summary: A synthetic support-ticket service, built through pnpm gatekeepers:scaffold as the second connection package: one queue per binding, its tickets read as observations and status changes proposed as approved actions. Synthetic data only; there is no real Tickets provider, so it is conformant, never reference.

resources.scope: One queue the account can see, fixed in the binding's props when the Workshop mints it; no session method takes a queue. A ticket of another queue is refused exactly as an unknown one (NOT_FOUND).

writes.notes: Refused at proposal and again at apply for a closed ticket or the status it already has (INVALID_STATE).

approval.rejection: Discards the staged action; a later apply of that id is refused.
approval.notes: Every status change is staged in the gatekeeper-kit action journal and submitted for approval; the agent waits for the decision (no simulation). Apply sends <binding id>:<action id> as the idempotency key, so a repeated or retried apply is answered by the provider without a second change, and the kit answers a repeated apply of an applied action as a no-op.

providerErrors.meaning: The queue or ticket does not exist or is outside the binding's scope; the two are indistinguishable.
The ticket changed after the write was proposed.
The ticket is closed, or already has the requested status.
The provider could not be reached or its response was lost. The action stays pending, and a retry sends the same idempotency key.

simulation.summary: None: reads show the provider's state only, and every write waits for the decision.

provider.name: Tickets (synthetic fake provider)
provider.notes: There is no real Tickets service; TicketsFakeProvider is the provider, so there is nothing to pin. A connector with a real provider pins its API here before it can be reference.
